Procedure Name.value: Zhang et al. (2022) Iron Meteorite LA-ICP-MS v1

Procedure Author.value: Zhang, Chabot, Rubin, Humayun et al.

Laboratory.value: Plasma Analytical Facility, Florida State University, Tallahassee FL, USA

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Zhang et al. (2022) GCA 323, 202–219; Humayun (2012) for standardization
Procedure Reference(s).value: Zhang et al. (2022) GCA 323, 202–219; Humayun (2012) for standardization

Coupling Description.cell: Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder [Section 2.5]
Coupling Description.value: Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder [Section 2.5]

Target Material.cell: Iron meteorite metal (kamacite + taenite); pyroxene-bearing pallasite metal

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Whole sample (polished specimen surface) > Region of interest (raster) — irons "were analyzed using a raster scan over a few millimeters" with a 50 μm beam, and compositions are reported as "raster averages" per specimen (Table 3, pp.4–5); Ge comes from a set of five 150 μm spots on five of the irons (p.4)
Sampling Unit Type.value: Whole sample (polished specimen surface) > Region of interest (raster)

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Polished metal slabs and thin sections; no acid treatment described
Sample Preparation Method.value: Polished metal slabs and thin sections; no acid treatment described

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: Representativeness of the exsolution banding — the raster "yielded more representative sampling of the kamacite-taenite banding", and where it "failed to yield useful Ge abundances for Klamath Falls ... To obtain more precise Ge, a set of five 150 μm spots were analyzed ... on five of the irons" (p.4)

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: Electron-microprobe mapping, for the pallasites only — "Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of the mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder were performed" on the Bruker instrument, producing Si, Al, Cr, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na, P and Ni maps "along with backscattered electron (BSE) maps" at 6 μm per pixel (pp.5–6); for the irons the paper states only that the rasters were "taken on polished surfaces" (p.5)
Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.value: Electron-microprobe mapping, for the pallasites only

Laser Manufacturer & Model.cell: ESI New Wave UP193FX (193 nm Nd:YAG frequency-quintupled solid state)
Laser Manufacturer & Model.value: ESI New Wave UP193FX (193 nm Nd:YAG frequency-quintupled solid state)

Detector Configuration.cell: Triple mode detection (pulse counting + analog + Faraday) at 65% duty cycle
Detector Configuration.value: Triple mode detection (pulse counting + analog + Faraday) at 65% duty cycle

Data Processing Software(s).cell: N (paper only states "standardization techniques followed those of Humayun (2012)"; no software named)

Laser Spot Geometry.cell: Raster: 50 µm circular beam spot; Spot (Ge): 150 µm circular

Laser Spot Path / Ablation Mode.cell: Raster area (2D mapping) for most irons; Spot (stationary) for Ge analysis on 5 irons

Laser Fluence (Energy Density).cell: N (no fluence reported; energy density characterized as "sufficient to resolve Ge from background argide")

Laser Pulse Duration.cell: N (UP193FX; ns solid-state; pulse duration not reported)

Raster Line Spacing (Mapping Only).cell: N (line spacing not explicitly stated; 50 µm spot scanned at 10 µm s⁻¹)

Oxide Production Method and Threshold.cell: N (not reported; no oxide proxy threshold stated)

Analysis Sequence.cell: Standards at start of session → raster unknowns → repeat → standards at end; separate session for Ge spot analyses
Analysis Sequence.value: Standards at start of session → raster unknowns → repeat → standards at end; separate session for Ge spot analyses

Target Species.cell: ³¹P, ⁵¹V, ⁵³Cr, ⁵⁵Mn, ⁵⁷Fe, ⁵⁹Co, ⁶⁰Ni, ⁶³Cu, ⁷¹Ga, ⁷⁴Ge, ⁷⁵As, ⁹⁵Mo, ¹⁰²Ru, ¹⁰³Rh, ¹⁰⁶Pd, ¹²⁰Sn, ¹²¹Sb, ¹⁸²W, ¹⁸⁵Re, ¹⁹⁰Os, ¹⁹³Ir, ¹⁹⁵Pt, ¹⁹⁷Au (23 elements; 31P, 51V, 53Cr, 55Mn, 57Fe, 59Co, 60Ni, 63Cu, 71Ga for spot Ge runs)

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Abundances of 23 elements in metal, with mixed units in one table — P, Fe, Co and Ni in mg/g, and V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Sn, Sb, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au in µg/g (Table 3, p.4). Values are reported as raster averages, with spot averages in Appendix 2; for Ge, Sb, Re, Os and Ir the reported value is "calculated from the mean of the spot average ... and the raster average" (p.4)

value.member: with mixed units in one table

Background Count Time.cell: N (gas blank measured before analyses but duration not reported)

Inter-Pass Data Dependency.cell: N (single raster acquisition; Ge spot separate session)

Number of Replicates.cell: N (number not stated explicitly; multiple irons analyzed)

Internal Standard Approach.cell: Standardization techniques followed those of Humayun (2012) [Section 2.2; specific IS approach not restated in this paper]

Internal Standard Element.cell: N (not stated in this paper; standardization follows Humayun (2012))

Elemental Fractionation Correction.cell: Multi-point external calibration using series of iron meteorite reference materials (North Chile Filomena as primary standard for Fe/Co/Ni/Cu/Ga/Ge/As/W/Au; Hoba for Ru/Rh/Pd/Re/Os/Ir/Pt; NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel for V/Cr/Fe/Co/Ni/Cu/As/Mo/W/Au)

Uncertainty Propagation Method.cell: Standard deviation (SD) across individual integration cycles of raster scans; uncertainty propagation not formally described

Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF).cell: N (no matrix offset correction; iron meteorite standards used to minimize matrix mismatch)

Signal Integration Interval Method.cell: N (raster averages; selection method not described)

Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.cell: N (raster scans; "failed to yield useful Ge abundances" for Klamath Falls noted — implying visual quality control)

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: Gas blank measured before each raster analysis; mean background subtracted
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: Gas blank measured before each raster analysis; mean background subtracted

Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Corre.cell: Applied: triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle (pulse counting + analog + Faraday); specific cross-calibration not described

value.value: triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle (pulse counting + analog + Faraday)

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: Yes — ⁹⁹Ru used instead of ¹⁰¹Ru to avoid ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni⁺ interference; isotope selection minimizes other interferences

Interfering Species.cell: ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni⁺ on ¹⁰¹Ru (most abundant Ru isotope → use ⁹⁹Ru instead)

Interference Correction Method.cell: Isotope selection: ⁹⁹Ru chosen over ¹⁰¹Ru; other isotopes chosen to minimize interference

Memory Effect Mitigation.cell: N (washout time between analyses not stated; sequential raster scans)

Normalization / Standards-Based Correcti.cell: External calibration with iron meteorite and NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel standards; no post-acquisition normalization described

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — the rule stated is one of combination rather than rejection: for Ge, Sb, Re, Os and Ir the reported value is "calculated from the mean of the spot average (Appendix 2) and the raster average in this table" (Table 3 note, p.4). No acceptance or rejection rule for individual results is stated. The exclusion of "Binya and Fitzwater Pass ... from the fractional-crystallization modeling of group IIIF" (p.5) is an interpretive exclusion downstream of the reported values, not a rule about which results make them

Combination Method.cell: Ge, Sb, Re, Os, Ir: mean of the spot average and the raster average; other: raster average — Table 3 title 'Compositions (raster averages)'; note: 'calculated from the mean of the spot average (Appendix 2) and the raster average in this table'

value.value: mean of the spot average and the raster average

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: North Chile Filomena (IIAB iron meteorite; Wasson et al. 1989) for Fe/Co/Ni/Cu/Ga/Ge/As/W/Au; Hoba (IVB; Walker et al. 2008) for Ru/Rh/Pd/Re/Os/Ir/Pt; NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel (Campbell & Humayun 2005) for V/Cr/Fe/Co/Ni/Cu/As/Mo/W/Au

Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.cell: Standards at start and end of session; external bracketing
Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.value: Standards at start and end of session; external bracketing

Detection Limit.cell: LODs not formally reported; all concentrations above detection limits except noted (Cr in some irons below LOD)

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Within-Session Analytical Precision and.cell: N (within-session precision not formally assessed; standard deviation across raster scans reported per element)

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: LA-ICP-MS concentrations agreed with NAA within ±40% for most elements (LA relative to NAA); within ±10% for Ni, Co, Ga; differences in W (4.39 vs 1.06 ng g⁻¹ for Cerro del Inca by LA vs INAA) and Au/As up to 30% — attributed to heterogeneous sampling scale difference between techniques

Additional Notes.cell: Raster scans used for main element dataset (23 elements); separate spot analyses on 5 irons for more precise Ge abundances (150 µm spot, 50 Hz, 20 s); two different analysis modes represent distinct protocols but are reported in same paper
Additional Notes.value: Raster scans used for main element dataset (23 elements); separate spot analyses on 5 irons for more precise Ge abundances (150 µm spot, 50 Hz, 20 s); two different analysis modes represent distinct protocols but are reported in same paper
